newsitem.title: USA: U.S. December S&P 500s end lower on dealer selling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. December S&P 500s end lower on dealer selling.

text.p: U.S. December Standard & Poor's 500 futures closed lower due to dealer selling, which resumed its pace after the U.S. bond futures market closed at 1400 CST/2000 GMT, floor traders said.
"Once bonds close, all the buying here stopped," one S&P futures floor trader said. "And S&Ps came down."

Some traders speculated asset allocation out of bonds and into stocks contributed to December S&Ps' modest flirtation with gains. One firm reportedly bought about 2,000 S&P futures, as U.S. bonds widened losses and the March T-bond contract tumbled below 114-00.

Despite the skittish activity in S&Ps, Nikkei futures clung to their gains. Traders said about 1,000 positions in December were rolled into the March contract, which becomes the lead contract month on Thursday, December 12.
December Nikkeis ended higher even as S&P 500s were hit by arbitrage sell programs.
One major U.S. firm also sold about 500 December S&P contracts in the last hour of trade. Traders noted arbitrage sell programs anywhere from a 0.50 to 0.70 point premium.
However, December held above its 2-1/2-week low of 739.55 ahead of key U.S. labor data on Friday.

At 0830 EST/1330 GMT, U.S. November nonfarm payrolls and the unemployment rate will be released. Payrolls are seen falling to 179,000, compared 210,000 in October, while the unemployment rate is seen holding steady at 5.2 percent.

December S&PS may be vulnerable to continued arbitrage sell programs before the number is released, as the contract ended Thursday's session at a narrow premium to the cash index. Fair value is at 1.25 points.

At the end of pit trade, December S&Ps were 2.30 points lower at 745.35, New Composites were 1.05 lower at 393.20, KBT Value Lines were unchanged at 683.75, Nikkei 225s were 295.0 higher at 20,900, Midcap 400s fell 0.35 at 256.20 and Nasdaq 100s were up 3.50 at 839.25.
